newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ZARAGOZA WANT REPLAY AFTER PENALTY CONTROVERSY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZARAGOZA WANT REPLAY AFTER PENALTY CONTROVERSY.

text.p: Zaragoza want to replay the last 20 minutes of Sunday's game with Barcelona which they had been leading 3-2 but ended up losing 5-3 after a linesman called a hotly-disputed penalty.

Television coverage suggests that linesman Rafael Guerrero mistook Zaragoza defender Xavier Aguado for teammate Jesus Solana, and that he may have been wrong to tell referee Enrique Mejuto to award a penalty.
Zaragoza have also sent football authorities a video of what they believe to be a series of bad refereeing decisions made against them this season.
The Spanish league disciplinary committee suspended neither Aguado nor Solana in its meeting on Tuesday.
The incident has become a major talking-point in Spain.
For many people Barcelona's Fernando Couto overreacted by falling to the ground when pushed from behind by Solana, a view apparently reflected even by Barcelona coach Bobby Robson.
"Couto was intelligent, but not Solana," said Robson.
Meanwhile the obscenity-charged conversation between the two officials is becoming the stuff of legend.

Atletico Madrid supporters chanted the more memorable phrases in Monday's game against Hercules, while a political comedy programme has put the dialogue in the mouths of puppets representing Premier Jose Maria Aznar and minister Francisco Alvarez Cascos.
Former Liverpool forward Michael Robinson, now a successful television commentator, also saw the comic side of the incident.
"If I were a bank robber, I'd like to have him as a witness," Robinson said of the linesman.

Linesman Guerrero has seen his life in a remote rural region disrupted by telephone threats. But he has turned down an offer of time off from his work as a caretaker at a school, which itself has been daubed with grafitti.
